title: Agent Benchmarks: What the Public Numbers Mean
summary: Agent benchmarks score models and scaffolds on real tasks in real environments: fixing repositories, serving simulated customers, browsing, operating a desktop or a terminal. This lesson explains how the main ones work, why their scores rose so fast, where they break, and how to read a reported agent result without being misled by scaffold, attempts or cost.
objectives: After this lesson you can explain how SWE-bench decides a task is resolved and why SWE-bench Verified and later SWE-bench Pro were created
Explain tau-bench's simulated users and database-state grading, and compute and interpret pass^k
Compare GAIA, WebArena, OSWorld and Terminal-Bench by environment, grading and what they test
Read an agent result critically: scaffold, number of attempts, cost, benchmark version and error bars
prerequisites: pass@k and pass^k from [/learn/agents/traces-and-evaluation](/learn/agents/traces-and-evaluation), and reading benchmarks critically from [/learn/evaluation/benchmarks-and-leaderboards](/learn/evaluation/benchmarks-and-leaderboards).
